correctness.rationale: The mathematical Finding is correct. With no clique vertex, domination forces selecting the whole nonempty independent part, whose induced graph has no perfect matching. With a clique vertex, domination is automatic. A perfect matching must send each of the b independent vertices to a different one of the a clique vertices; this is sufficient when a+b is even, since the remaining clique vertices pair off. This proves the coefficients by independent binomial choices, including r=1 and n=1. Every edge alone dominates and every nonempty paired-dominating set contains a matching edge, proving both size-two conclusions. The frozen proof is all-orders; the inspected verify.py and recorded finite output are not needed as proof and the frozen script was not run. The false family assertion at RESULT.md line 62 affects the prior-work comparison, not the theorem.

evidence: The prior formula subtracts from all 2q-subsets those with an occupancy greater than q in any part. Here only I can have such an occupancy, so the specialization is binom(r+n,2q) minus the sum of binom(n,j)binom(r,2q-j) for q<j<=min(n,2q).
